# CRW-1028 verifier round 3: reader and consumer gaps the independent verifier found in the round 2 head (210962646).
# Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-1028-v3-01 | U
--why cp -r -t bin evil/. copies the contents of evil into bin itself: bin/tool is the copied program.
--file bin/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -r -t bin evil/.; bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v3-02 | U
--why cp -r --target-directory=bin evil/. fills bin itself, then a shell runs bin/tool as its script operand: the body the guards read is stale.
--file bin/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -r --target-directory=bin evil/.; bash bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v3-03 | U
--why cp -r evil/. bin (the plain form) fills bin itself; the script operand bin/tool is the copied file.
--file bin/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -r evil/. bin; bash bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v3-04 | B
--why Control: the copy of evil/. fills bin, and the script the text runs is other/tool, outside it.
--file other/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -r -t bin evil/.; bash other/tool

=== CRW-1028-v3-05 | U
--why A script run before another rewrites it (writer.sh overwrites post.sh): the later sibling runs the new body, not the one the guards read.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file writer.sh
cat evil.sh > post.sh
--cmd
bash writer.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v3-06 | U
--why A nested script's write (outer.sh runs writer.sh, which overwrites post.sh) reaches a later sibling of the outer script.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file writer.sh
cat evil.sh > post.sh
--file outer.sh
bash writer.sh
--cmd
bash outer.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v3-07 | U
--why Siblings inside a script body: pair.sh runs writer.sh, then post.sh, which writer.sh overwrote.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file writer.sh
cat evil.sh > post.sh
--file pair.sh
bash writer.sh; bash post.sh
--cmd
bash pair.sh

=== CRW-1028-v3-08 | U
--why A script that writes a destination the reader cannot name may write the later sibling script: an unknown write.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file writer.sh
cat evil.sh > "$DEST"
--cmd
bash writer.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v3-09 | B
--why Control: the earlier script writes another file (other.sh), so the later sibling post.sh is the body the guards read.
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file writer.sh
cat evil.sh > other.sh
--cmd
bash writer.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v3-10 | W | deviation=B
--why Deferred to CRW-900 (900c): open bound through a module attribute (f=io.open) writes into the memory root; the Python destination reader does not follow the binding, so the gate sees no write.
--cmd
python3 -c "import io; f=io.open; f('{MEMORY}/target','w').write('x')"

=== CRW-1028-v3-11 | W | deviation=B
--why Deferred to CRW-900 (900c): open bound by a from-import alias (from io import open as o) writes into the memory root; the Python destination reader does not follow the alias.
--cmd
python3 -c "from io import open as o; o('{MEMORY}/target','w').write('x')"

=== CRW-1028-v3-12 | T
--why Control: a script's own write to a destination the reader cannot name is an unknown write for the scripts after it, not a rewrite of the script itself.
--file build.sh
cat post.sh > "$OUT"
echo done
--file post.sh
echo clean
--cmd
bash build.sh
